label: <DEL> step of short (L=3) sequences, esp. starting with e/x/h/g
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (phase 1, recall_idx 0), almost entirely in L=3 sequences (90% of active steps, 93% of mass; remainder L=4). Within L=3 it fires on only ~13% of delimiters; the strongest modulator is the first original token (the token about to be output): e and x give the highest rate and top activations, then h, g, r, n. Later tokens matter weakly (prev_tok d/w/b/u favored; digits in the sequence suppress it). Never fires in the original or copy phases or for L>=5. Dev: (phase==1)&(L==3) has recall 0.90/mass 0.93 but precision 0.13; adding first_tok in {e,x,h,g} gives P 0.58, R 0.53, F1 0.55, mass 0.65. The residual token dependence looks graded/distributed rather than a clean rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: e, x, h, r, g, n; least: p, -, z, b) and the previous input (most: u, d, b, w, 2, 3; least: j, n, a, t); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=3, L=3, t=3.
